Subject: Initial questions on data capture/derivative treatment for DPA

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick connect yesterday. We have two procurement checkpoints before we can move the DPA to legal review: a concise statement on how Redwood treats prompts + generated outputs for model improvement, and a list of subprocessors with residency (onshore/offshore) so we can assess transfer risk. Topline asks from our security/privacy team are below — I put the spreadsheet with the questionnaire attached.

Key questions (short form):
- Does Redwood retain prompts/responses beyond request processing? If yes: retention period and how to disable or shorten.
- Can customer data be excluded from all model-improvement pipelines (a no-training commitment)? What operational evidence do you provide?
- Who are your subprocessors today and which regions do they operate in? Any planned migrations in the next 90 days?
- For customers requiring onshore-only handling, what options exist (SFTP exports, onshore KMS, VPC private deployment)?
- How do you map prompt/response ownership vs derived model improvements or derivatives?

We need answerable bullets for our DPA team so they can draft the redline. If you have a short statement/template (PDF or one-pager) we can include that as an exhibit.

Attachment: HealthNova-llm-dpa-questions.xlsx (xlsx)

Appreciate it — Lukas

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Lukas —

Thanks for the clear checklist and the spreadsheet. Below are concise answers your DPA team can use as bullets; I copied David (ops/legal liaison) and Kimberly (privacy policy) for any legal phrasing tweaks. Short versions first, then operational notes.

1) Retention of prompts/responses
- By default, Redwood retains request logs and raw prompt/response payloads for 30 days to support debugging, billing, and abuse detection.
- Customers can opt into shorter retention windows (down to 0 days) or enable ephemeral-mode where content is not persisted beyond the immediate request.
- For contractual commitments we offer an enforceable retention SLA (e.g., 0/7/30 days) documented in the DPA exhibit.

2) No-training / model-improvement exclusion
- Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts or responses for model improvement unless an explicit opt-in is provided (opt-in is per-account and auditable).
- We can provide a signed No-Training Commitment Statement as a DPA exhibit. See attached: Redwood-No-Training-Commitment-Statement.pdf
- Operational evidence: periodic attestation logs, subprocessor access logs, and a snapshot of the model-improvement pipeline showing excluded namespaces.

3) Subprocessors and residency
- Current subprocessor list attached: redwood_subprocessors_q3_2026.csv (includes region and purpose).
- Short-term migrations (next 90 days): none planned that would affect onshore-only customers; any change triggers a 30-day notice and risk assessment.

4) Onshore-only handling options
- Hosted customers: onshore routing and KMS residency available for enterprise contracts; we can provide onshore SFTP export of raw request logs on demand.
- Private/Dedicated customers: full control plane in-customer VPC or on-premise option.
- We maintain an onshore KMS matrix; see KMS-location-matrix.pdf (attached).

5) Ownership / derivatives
- Customer retains ownership of their input data and any outputs they generate (standard contractual language: customer owns output IP).
- Redwood will not assert rights to derived models trained on customer data under the no-training commitment.
- We can include a carve-out clause for derivative models in the DPA language.

Attachments: Redwood-No-Training-Commitment-Statement.pdf (pdf), redwood_subprocessors_q3_2026.csv (csv), KMS-location-matrix.pdf (pdf)

If that looks good, we can move to a short exhibit for the DPA and provide an operations evidence pack (ops-evidence-pack-HealthNova.zip) that contains the exportable logs, attestation, and a redacted pipeline diagram. David/ Kimberly — please flag if any of the bullets need stronger legal wording.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Strategy
Redwood Inference

This is helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups before we hand to procurement:
- Can you provide a short, signed PDF statement (your No-Training Commitment) that we can attach to the DPA as an exhibit? The wording should be explicit: "Redwood will not use Customer data for model training or improvements unless Customer provides explicit, auditable opt-in."
- For the ops evidence pack: we need an indication of where KMS keys are resident for onshore options (US-only keys) and the SFTP export process (frequency, retention of the exported copies).
- Please also include a simple attestation timeline: how often Redwood will re-attest subprocessor access and that logging will be retained for at least 90 days for audit.

If you can drop these into a single ZIP and point us to the HubSpot deal record, procurement can attach and schedule a legal review call.

Best — Lukas
